style.vernacular: A brick city: four- to five-storey perimeter blocks of yellow and red brick with steep red clay-tile or flat tar roofs around courtyards in the centre; Functionalist and 1960s-70s concrete and brick housing estates and prefabricated low-rise settlements in the suburbs; whitewashed medieval village churches with red-tile roofs and stepped gables; white or yellow-washed half-timbered inns and farm buildings, some thatched; glass, steel and aluminium offices, malls and arenas in Orestad and the western suburbs. Green verdigris copper spires and roofs mark civic and church towers; beech, lime and lawns everywhere.
style.ornament: stepped (crow-step) gables and whitewashed walls on village churches; slate roofs with copper-clad spires; yellow-brick stringcourses and white-framed windows on perimeter blocks; black half-timbering on inns; Nordic Classicism and Functionalist flat roofs with horizontal windows; coastal fort earthworks with concrete casemates; bicycle racks and cobbled lanes.
